original_question: For a given open or generalized billiard system, can the survival probability P(t) be computed exactly, or at least expanded for large t beyond its leading asymptotic term?
target_in_paper: Problem 11.17 ("Exact expansions") in Section 11.6 ("Discussion"). It asks, in substance, whether for a fixed open (generalised) billiard problem the survival probability P(t) can be obtained exactly, or at least asymptotically expanded beyond its leading large-t term. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core target almost exactly: it names the survival probability P(t), asks for exact formulae or large-t asymptotics, and explicitly asks for terms beyond the leading asymptotic behaviour. That is very close to the official wording of Problem 11.17. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
missing_details: The paper defines the survival probability by first defining the survivor set Omega_t = {x in Omega : Phi^s(x) is not in H for all s in (0,t]}, and then setting P(t) = mu_0(Omega_t). Your draft leaves Omega, H, Phi^t, Omega_t, and mu_0 implicit. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The problem is posed for a specified open billiard problem together with an initial probability measure mu_0 at time t = 0; without naming that initial measure, the question is not fully stand-alone. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The hole H is part of the data: it may have several components, may lie on the boundary or in the interior, and its location and relative size h affect P(t). Your draft does not mention the hole explicitly. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

For billiards, the paper takes continuous time as the default unless otherwise stated, even though some calculations are done via the collision map. So 'large t' should be read in that flow-based sense here. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The adjective 'generalised' is not meant in an unrestricted way; the immediately preceding Problem 11.16 gives the intended nearby scope: soft wall potentials, external fields, dissipative and/or stochastic scattering, or time-dependent boundaries. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The nearby discussion narrows the most promising cases to integrable and dispersing billiards, motivated by earlier examples where only leading behaviour or small-hole expansions are known. Adding this makes the question sharper and more faithful to the paper's intent. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))

The surrounding motivation emphasizes recurrent and periodic-orbit structure as the mechanism governing long-time survival, especially when the initial measure is not supported on the hole; this explains why the paper asks specifically about lower-order terms beyond the leading asymptotic. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
refined_question: Fix an open billiard flow Phi^t on phase space Omega with a piecewise smooth hole H subset Omega (or, in the immediately preceding generalised setting, one of the billiard models with soft walls, external fields, dissipative/stochastic scattering, or time-dependent boundaries), and let Omega_t = {x in Omega : Phi^s(x) is not in H for all s in (0,t]} and P(t) = mu_0(Omega_t) for a prescribed initial probability measure mu_0 at time t = 0. For that fixed billiard problem, can the survival probability P(t) be computed exactly, or at least asymptotically expanded as t tends to infinity beyond its leading term, particularly in the integrable and dispersing cases singled out by the paper? ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
justification: The draft is already a near-paraphrase of Problem 11.17, so the right refinement is not to broaden it but to import the notation and scope from Section 11.3 and the nearby discussion. Section 11.3 supplies the formal definitions of the hole H, survivor set Omega_t, initial measure mu_0, and survival probability P(t) = mu_0(Omega_t). Section 11.4 explains why integrable and dispersing billiards are the natural first targets by pointing to exact leading-order information for the open circle, small-hole expansions for dispersing billiards, and an explicit leading coefficient for the stadium. Section 11.6 then formulates the open problem precisely as asking for exact expressions or asymptotic expansions beyond the leading term. ([people.maths.bris.ac.uk](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~macpd/open/open.pdf))
